NeuTTS-Air|en: [Language: English | Indo-European (Germanic) | Latin-script | stress-timed | non-tonal] Architecturally, NeuTTS-Air is built around a non-autoregressive transformer with neural codec. The mel-or-token predictor (transformer acoustic model paired with a distilled, low-latency decoder; targets ~200 ms synthesis latency) outputs discrete codec tokens. This representation is subsequently inverted to waveform by neural audio codec (HiFi-GAN-class decoder). English TTS must handle unstressed vowel reduction, heterogeneous prosodic phrasing, and dialectal variation; artifacts most frequently appear in fricatives and phrase boundaries.

[Language: English | Indo-European (Germanic) | Latin-script | stress-timed | non-tonal] A detection-oriented look at NeuTTS-Air starts from what it leaves in the output, not what it is. Analysts will spot three fingerprints in its output: oversmoothed spectrograms; rigid timing; and pitch quantisation. They follow from the non-autoregressive transformer with neural codec: the neural audio codec (HiFi-GAN-class decoder) handles waveform reconstruction. Corpus: multi-speaker speech datasets; language coverage: many languages.

OpenVoiceV2|en: [Language: English | Indo-European (Germanic) | Latin-script | stress-timed | non-tonal] Its acoustic stage, MeloTTS-based VITS base generates stylised speech; lightweight encoder-decoder tone-color converter transfers target speaker timbre, emits linear/mel spectrogram + tone-color embedding. From there, GAN-based waveform generator inside MeloTTS base produces the output waveform. Trained on large-scale multilingual speech collections, it operates zero-shot clone (seconds of reference) over multilingual (en, es, fr, zh, ja, ko). English TTS must handle unstressed vowel reduction, heterogeneous prosodic phrasing, and dialectal variation; artifacts most frequently appear in fricatives and phrase boundaries.

[Language: English | Indo-European (Germanic) | Latin-script | stress-timed | non-tonal] Signal-analysis view of OpenVoiceV2: the fingerprint is more useful than the block diagram. Analysts will spot three fingerprints in its output: phase distortion in unvoiced consonants from tone-color conversion; pitch-shifting artifacts; and over-regularised spectral envelopes. These stem from an underlying two-stage pipeline (base VITS TTS + tone-color converter) with GAN-based waveform generator inside MeloTTS base reconstructing the waveform. Corpus: large-scale multilingual speech collections; language coverage: multilingual (en, es, fr, zh, ja, ko).
